issue.body:
## Bug

When a user uses Ctrl-C during `click.prompt()`, this may cause an unhandled exception. Seen during CI on an Ubuntu 22.04 arm github runner. The same test on Ubuntu 22.04 x64, macOS arm, Windows x64/arm succeeded. This is likely to be a race that doesn't pop up every time

```
    | --- tty: Ctrl+C aborts at a prompt ---
    | spawn /home/runner/work/ethstaker-deposit-cli/ethstaker-deposit-cli/ethstaker_deposit-cli-c082a10-linux-arm64/deposit --language english --ignore_connectivity generate-mnemonic
    | Please choose the language of the mnemonic word list [1. 简体中文, 2. 繁體中文, 3. čeština, 4. English, 5. Français, 6. Italiano, 7. 日本語, 8. 한국어, 9. Português, 10. Español]:  [english]: ^CTraceback (most recent call last):
    |   File "click/core.py", line 1490, in main
    |   File "click/core.py", line 1968, in invoke
    |   File "click/core.py", line 1300, in make_context
    |   File "click/core.py", line 1311, in parse_args
    |   File "click/core.py", line 2686, in handle_parse_result
    |   File "click/core.py", line 3508, in consume_value
    |   File "ethstaker_deposit/utils/click.py", line 62, in prompt_for_value
    |   File "click/core.py", line 3372, in prompt_for_value
    |   File "click/termui.py", line 218, in prompt
    |   File "click/termui.py", line 201, in prompt_func
    | click.exceptions.Abort
    | 
    | During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
    | 
    | Traceback (most recent call last):
    |   File "deposit.py", line 128, in <module>
    |   File "deposit.py", line 121, in run
    |   File "click/core.py", line 1569, in __call__
    |   File "click/core.py", line 1532, in main
    |   File "click/utils.py", line 337, in echo
    |   File "click/_compat.py", line 509, in should_strip_ansi
    |   File "click/_compat.py", line 578, in isatty
    | KeyboardInterrupt
    | [PYI-3853:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'deposit' due to unhandled exception!
    | 
    | [TEST FAIL] Unexpected EOF while waiting for: Aborted
```

## Replication

Probably a `click.prompt()` with Ctrl-C on a slower machine, run often enough to eventually trigger this race condition. In our case it was the free github `ubuntu-22.04-arm` runner.

## Expected

click handles the KeyboardInterrupt exception gracefully, regardless of timing or architecture.

Environment:

- Python version: 3.14
- Click version: 8.4.2
issue.title: `KeyboardInterrupt` during `click.prompt()` can race

<!--
This issue tracker is a tool to address bugs in Click itself. Please use
GitHub Discussions or the Pallets Discord for questions about your own code.

Replace this comment with a clear outline of what the bug is.
-->
I had failing unit tests after upgrading to click 8.4.1. I was able to address some 
by using `runner.invoke(cmd, color=False)`, but that didn't help for commands
that use `click.confirm()`

<!--
Describe how to replicate the bug.

Include a minimal reproducible example that demonstrates the bug.
Include the full traceback if there was an exception.
-->

This test script `test_repro.py` replicates the issue.
```
import click
from click.testing import CliRunner


@click.command()
def cmd():
    click.echo(click.style('Hello World!', fg='green'))


@click.command()
def cmd_confirm():
    click.confirm(click.style('Hello World!', fg='green'), abort=True)


def test_echo_strips_ansi_with_color_false():
    runner = CliRunner()
    result = runner.invoke(cmd, color=False)
    assert result.output == "Hello World!\n"


def test_confirm_strips_ansi_with_color_false():
    runner = CliRunner()
    result = runner.invoke(cmd_confirm, input="Y", color=False)
    assert result.output == "Hello World! [y/N]: Y\n"  # FAILS: ANSI codes present
```

With click 8.3.3 both tests pass. With click 8.4.0 and 8.4.1, the `test_confirm_strips_ansi_with_color_false` test fails:

```
uvx --with click==8.4 pytest test_repro.py
...
================================================ FAILURES ================================================
_______________________________ test_confirm_strips_ansi_with_color_false ________________________________

    def test_confirm_strips_ansi_with_color_false():
        runner = CliRunner()
        result = runner.invoke(cmd_confirm, input="Y", color=False)
>       assert result.output == "Hello World! [y/N]: Y\n"  # FAILS: ANSI codes present
```

<!--
Describe the expected behavior that should have happened but didn't.
-->
The ansi codes should be stripped when running click.confirm, as they are for click.echo.

Environment:

- Python version: 3.13
- Click version: 8.4.1
- MacOS
issue.title: ANSI codes not stripped from click.confirm after upgrading to click 8.4

issue.body:
Using a `click.progressbar` with:
- `update_min_steps` which isn't a divisor of `length`
- `show_pos=True`

won't show full completion at the end. This can be reproduced as follows:

```python
import time

import click

with click.progressbar(
    range(20),
    show_pos=True,
    update_min_steps=7,
) as bar:
    for i in bar:
        time.sleep(0.1)
```

with (final) output in the terminal

```text
  [####################################]  14/20          
```

**Expected behaviour**: I had expected the output to show `20/20` at the end.
This would be consistent with the default percentage formatting, as can be seen by commenting the line `show_pos=True` and re-running the reproduction:

```text
  [####################################]  100%          
```

Environment:

- Python version: tested with 3.12.3 and 3.14.3
- Click version: 8.4.1
issue.title: `click.progressbar` doesn't show full completion when using `show_pos=True` combined with `update_min_steps`

issue.body:
Hi,
when developing psutil on Windows, I do it by mapping `X:` to a sshfs share, so from Linux I can SSH into Windows and run tests there. Problem: pytest ignores the file I pass and collects everything:

```
$ python -m pytest tests/test_memleaks.py --collect-only -o addopts=""
platform win32 -- Python 3.14.6, pytest-9.1.1, pluggy-1.6.0
rootdir: X:\svn\psutil
collected 961 items
```

That file ( tests/test_memleaks.py ) has 130 tests, while 961 is the whole repo. Using absolute paths does the same.

I think the culprit is `samefile_nofollow()`, which `Session.collect()` falls back to on Windows when two paths don't compare equal. On this drive every file has `st_ino == 0`, so it says any two files are the same one:

```
$ python -c "
import os
a = os.stat('tests/test_memleaks.py')
b = os.stat('tests/test_process.py')
print(a.st_dev, a.st_ino)
print(b.st_dev, b.st_ino)
print(os.path.samestat(a, b))
"
3816903231 0
3816903231 0
True
```

So every node matches, nothing gets pruned, and I get the whole tree. The name parts still work, which fits: `::` filtering happens after the path level.

```
$ python -m pytest "tests/test_memleaks.py::TestProcess" --collect-only -q
tests/test_windows.py::TestProcess::test_wait
175 tests collected
```

That's `TestProcess` from every file, not the one I asked for.

Maybe the fallback should just bail out when either `st_ino` is 0, since it can't tell anything apart at that point:

```diff
 def samefile_nofollow(p1: Path, p2: Path) -> bool:
-    return os.path.samestat(p1.lstat(), p2.lstat())
+    s1, s2 = p1.lstat(), p2.lstat()
+    if not s1.st_ino or not s2.st_ino:
+        return False
+    return os.path.samestat(s1, s2)
```

Returning `False` falls back to plain path comparison, which is what the other platforms do anyway. The short-path case this was added for (#11895) is on local NTFS, so it keeps working.

`-m` and `-k` work fine. Anything taking a path (`--ignore`, `--deselect`, plain args) doesn't.
issue.title: (Windows) passing a file path collects the whole suite, on a network drive where st_ino is 0

issue.body:
### Initial Checks

- [X] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

`ser_json_temporal` landed in v2.12 and controls how `datetime`, `date`, `time` and `timedelta` are serialized to JSON. `GenerateJsonSchema` was never told about it, so a `mode='serialization'` schema still says these fields are strings even when `model_dump_json()` writes numbers.

With `ser_json_temporal='seconds'` (same with `'milliseconds'`), every temporal field is affected:

```
schema:  {'dt': {'type': 'string', 'format': 'date-time'}, 'td': {'type': 'string', 'format': 'duration'}}
dump:    {'dt': 1577836800.0, 'td': 86400.0}
```

Running that payload through a JSON Schema validator fails with `1577836800.0 is not of type 'string'`, so the schema pydantic publishes rejects the output pydantic itself just produced. `date_schema`, `time_schema` and `datetime_schema` read no config at all right now.

There is a second mismatch that goes the other way, on `timedelta`. `timedelta_schema` only looks at the older `ser_json_timedelta` setting. The docs for `ser_json_temporal` say it takes precedence over `ser_json_timedelta`, and pydantic-core implements exactly that: `SerializationConfig::from_config` and `TimeDeltaSerializer::build` both check whether `ser_json_temporal` is present in the config before falling back to `ser_json_timedelta`. The JSON schema layer does not, so setting `ser_json_temporal='iso8601'` together with `ser_json_timedelta='float'` gives you the reverse problem:

```
schema:  {'td': {'type': 'number'}}
dump:    {'td': 'P1D'}
```

For anyone generating an OpenAPI document from a model this is a silent wrong answer rather than a crash, which is probably why it has gone unnoticed since the setting was added.

I have a patch that mirrors the pydantic-core resolution in the four temporal schema methods, plus tests. Happy to open a PR if you want to assign this to me.

### Example Code

```Python
import json
from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


class Numeric(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(ser_json_temporal='seconds')

    dt: datetime
    d: date
    t: time
    td: timedelta


model = Numeric(dt=datetime(2020, 1, 1), d=date(2020, 1, 1), t=time(12, 0), td=timedelta(days=1))

print(Numeric.model_json_schema(mode='serialization')['properties'])
#> {'dt': {'format': 'date-time', 'title': 'Dt', 'type': 'string'},
#>  'd': {'format': 'date', 'title': 'D', 'type': 'string'},
#>  't': {'format': 'time', 'title': 'T', 'type': 'string'},
#>  'td': {'format': 'duration', 'title': 'Td', 'type': 'string'}}

print(json.loads(model.model_dump_json()))
#> {'dt': 1577836800.0, 'd': 1577836800.0, 't': 43200.0, 'td': 86400.0}


# The timedelta precedence case, wrong in the opposite direction:
class Precedence(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(ser_json_temporal='iso8601', ser_json_timedelta='float')

    td: timedelta


print(Precedence.model_json_schema(mode='serialization')['properties'])
#> {'td': {'title': 'Td', 'type': 'number'}}

print(json.loads(Precedence(td=timedelta(days=1)).model_dump_json()))
#> {'td': 'P1D'}
```

### Python, Pydantic & OS Version

```Text
             pydantic version: 2.13.4
        pydantic-core version: 2.46.4
          pydantic-core build: profile=release pgo=false
               python version: 3.12.13 (main, May 10 2026, 19:20:41) [Clang 22.1.3 ]
                     platform: macOS-15.7.4-arm64-arm-64bit
             related packages: typing_extensions-4.16.0
                       commit: unknown
```

Also reproduces on `main` (2.14.0b1 / pydantic-core 2.48.0).
issue.title: JSON Schema ignores `ser_json_temporal`, so serialization schemas contradict `model_dump_json()` output

issue.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed the bug exists on the latest version of pydantic (2.13.4) and on current `main`.

### Python Version

3.13.14

### Pydantic Version

pydantic 2.13.4 / pydantic-core (latest from pip at time of report)

### Description

A model field annotated `SecretStr` with an **unvalidated `None` default** crashes serialization to JSON. Per [models docs](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/models/), field defaults are only validated when `validate_default=True`, so constructing such a model without arguments is legal — and every other scalar annotation serializes the unvalidated default as `null`. For `SecretStr`, however, `model_dump_json()` raises instead.

Note this is specific to the JSON path and to the *non-nullable* annotation:
* `model_dump()` (python mode) returns `None` fine;
* `Optional[SecretStr] = None` dumps to JSON correctly (`{"s":null}`);
* a control field `n: int = None` also dumps fine — so only the combination "non-nullable SecretStr + None default + JSON serializer" hits the broken path.

### Example Code

```python
import warnings
from typing import Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel, SecretStr

class M(BaseModel):
    n: int = None          # same pattern, control group
    s: SecretStr = None    # crashes

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    print(M().model_dump())          # {'n': None, 's': None}  -- OK
    try:
        print(M().model_dump_json())
    except Exception as e:
        print(type(e).__name__, "|", e)
    print("warnings emitted:", len(w))

class O(BaseModel):
    s: Optional[SecretStr] = None

print(O().model_dump_json())         # {"s":null} -- OK
```

### Actual behavior

```
{'n': None, 's': None}
PydanticSerializationError | Error calling function '_serialize_secret_field': AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get_secret_value'
warnings emitted: 0
{"s":null}
```

The exception escapes even though the value mismatch is exactly the situation the serialization layer normally degrades gracefully on (serialize as-is / warn). No `UserWarning` about the mismatched default is emitted either.

Looking at `_serialize_secret_field`, it calls `.get_secret_value()` unconditionally when the serializer runs with `when_used='always'`; there is no guard for `value is None` on a non-optional annotation, while core handles `None` defaults for other types before user serializers are reached.

### Expected behavior

Either of the consistent-with-everything-else outcomes:

1. serialize the unvalidated default as `null`: `{"n":null,"s":null}` (matching how `int = None`, `str = None` etc. behave), or
2. at minimum emit the standard serialization-mismatch `UserWarning` instead of raising an internal `AttributeError` wrapped into `PydanticSerializationError`.

The current traceback points users at pydantic internals rather than their own model definition.
issue.title: model_dump_json crashes on a SecretStr field with an unvalidated None default (internal AttributeError instead of null/warning)

issue.body:
### Initial Checks

- [x] I confirm that I'm using Pydantic V2

### Description

Since v2.11, `@validate_call(config=ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True))` no longer allows passing an aliased parameter by its name — the same config on a `BaseModel` works, and the [`populate_by_name` docs](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/api/config/#pydantic.config.ConfigDict.populate_by_name) say it is strictly equivalent to `validate_by_name=True, validate_by_alias=True` (deprecated in v3, but still supported). Works on 2.10.6; broken on 2.11.x, 2.12.x, and `main`.

A worse variant: `@validate_call(config=ConfigDict(validate_by_alias=False))` makes the aliased parameter impossible to provide at all (both name and alias raise), even though #11503 made `validate_by_alias=False` implicitly enable `validate_by_name`.

Root cause: `_arguments_schema()`/`_arguments_v3_schema()` embed `validate_by_name=self._config_wrapper.validate_by_name` into the core schema (`_generate_schema.py:2081/2149`), reading the raw config key. The backwards-compatibility patch mapping `populate_by_name` → `validate_by_name` only runs inside `ConfigWrapper.core_config()`, and pydantic-core gives the schema-embedded value precedence over the validator config, so the patched core config is never consulted. Models are unaffected because model-fields schemas don't embed the flag.

I have a fix ready and will open a PR.

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Annotated
from pydantic import Field, validate_call

@validate_call(config=dict(populate_by_name=True))
def f(a: Annotated[int, Field(alias='b')]) -> int:
    return a

f(b=1)  # OK
f(a=1)  # ValidationError: Unexpected keyword argument
```

### Python, Pydantic & OS Version

```text
             pydantic version: 2.14.0b1
        pydantic-core version: 2.48.0
          pydantic-core build: profile=release pgo=false
               python version: 3.11.14 (main, Oct  9 2025, 16:16:55) [Clang 17.0.0 (clang-1700.4.4.1)]
                     platform: macOS-26.5.2-arm64-arm-64bit
             related packages: typing_extensions-4.16.0
                       commit: 2151025
```

(also reproduced on released pydantic 2.11.10 and 2.12.5; not reproducible on 2.10.6)
issue.title: `populate_by_name` (and implicit `validate_by_name` when `validate_by_alias=False`) is ignored by `@validate_call`

issue.body:
Reported downstream in Giskard-AI/giskard#2719 (breaks `import giskard.checks`); repro and analysis below. The report was drafted jointly with @davidberenstein1957, who invited it to be filed upstream as-is.

### Description

`_generate_schema.match_type` added an unguarded dict lookup in 2.14 that assumes the annotation object is hashable. It is not, for a PEP 695 type alias with a `ParamSpec` parameterized by an empty list. Schema building for any model containing such an annotation crashes.

This is a regression: the same code builds fine on 2.13.4.

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Any
from pydantic import BaseModel

type Alias[**P, R] = Any

class M(BaseModel):
    f: Alias[[], int] | None = None
```

Raises immediately at class-definition time:

```
File ".../pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py", line 1127, in match_type
    if origin is not None and (aliased_obj := typing_objects.DEPRECATED_ALIASES.get(obj)):
TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'
```

### Mechanism

`Alias[[], int]` is a `types.GenericAlias` whose `__args__` is `([], int)`. Hashing the alias hashes that tuple, which contains a `list` — so it is unhashable. The line at `_generate_schema.py:1127`

```python
if origin is not None and (aliased_obj := typing_objects.DEPRECATED_ALIASES.get(obj)):
```

calls `.get(obj)` without checking that `obj` can be hashed. `dict.get` propagates the `TypeError` rather than treating an unhashable key as absent.

### Suggested fix

Guard the lookup, e.g.

```python
if origin is not None and isinstance(obj, Hashable) and (aliased_obj := typing_objects.DEPRECATED_ALIASES.get(obj)):
```

or wrap it in `try/except TypeError`. An unhashable object cannot be a `DEPRECATED_ALIASES` key by construction, so skipping the lookup is always correct.

### Python, Pydantic & OS Version

- pydantic 2.14.0b1 (fails) / 2.13.4 (works)
- Python 3.12.13
- Reproduced on Linux and macOS

### Real-world impact

Hit in [giskard-oss](https://github.com/Giskard-AI/giskard-oss), where `type GeneratorType[**P, R, S] = ...` parameterized as `GeneratorType[[], InputType, None]` makes `import giskard.checks` fail outright under 2.14.0b1. Instrumenting `match_type` confirms the offending object:

```
OFFENDING obj  = GeneratorType[[], InputType, None]
OFFENDING type = <class 'types.GenericAlias'>
OFFENDING args = ([], InputType, None)
```

There is no workaround on the library side short of pinning `pydantic<2.14` (done in Giskard-AI/giskard#2752), which is what downstream has had to do.
issue.title: TypeError: unhashable type: 'list' in match_type for PEP 695 aliases with a ParamSpec (regression in 2.14.0b1)
